topic: Unified iterative RAG stopping and provenance control under distribution shift: controllers combining structured evidence sufficiency with temporal/version-aware provenance and calibrated or conformal risk-controlled stopping, including permission-aware access and bounded retrieval budgets

gaps.description: Structured gap representations remain insufficiently validated for temporal constraints, multi-entity joins, and complex compositional evidence requirements; the corpus contains structured-gap, temporal-retrieval, and query-planning methods, but no admitted study evaluates these capabilities together.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "structured evidence gap" temporal constraints multi-entity joins compositional retrieval iterative RAG
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-4. The admitted literature separately supports structured missing-evidence representations, temporal retrieval, and compositional/query-planning methods, but does not jointly evaluate structured gaps with temporal constraints, multi-entity joins, and complex compositional evidence requirements.

gaps.description: No admitted study validates an iterative evidence-gap retrieval loop that jointly preserves document-version lineage, freshness or effective-time validity, and structured sufficiency decisions.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "version-aware retrieval" temporal provenance iterative RAG document lineage freshness effective-time sufficiency
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-4. VersionRAG, temporal retrieval, Temporal GraphRAG, SentryLine, S2G-RAG, and FAIR-RAG cover relevant subsets, but the admitted corpus does not validate their required combination in one iterative evidence-gap loop.

gaps.description: Stopping reliability under domain shift remains open: sufficiency, confidence, conformal, stability, and drift-adaptive calibration signals are evaluated in separate studies, but no admitted study provides a general bounded-risk iterative-RAG stopping guarantee under distribution shift.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "iterative RAG" calibrated stopping domain shift conformal risk control selective prediction adaptive retrieval
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-4. MiCP and the admitted conformal-calibration literature address multi-turn stopping or several forms of distribution shift, but no admitted study establishes a general bounded-risk iterative-RAG stopping guarantee that remains controlled under shift.

gaps.description: The corpus does not test a bounded replenishment loop in which unauthorized candidates are filtered through native IAM, evidence sufficiency is reassessed, and another permission-constrained query is issued when authorized evidence remains incomplete.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by implementing a reference controller against one or more native IAM/RBAC-capable retrieval backends. Instrument each iteration as retrieve -> authorize/filter -> reassess structured sufficiency -> formulate permission-constrained replenishment query -> stop on sufficiency or budget. Benchmark correctness, leakage prevention, number of replenishment rounds, recall over authorized evidence, and latency under controlled permission scenarios.

gaps.description: The evaluated systems do not jointly distinguish empty retrieval, authorization denial, unavailable source, unsupported extraction, exhausted budget, and true negative evidence as separate terminal or retry conditions.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by defining an explicit retrieval outcome/error taxonomy and controller state machine with distinct machine-readable statuses for empty retrieval, access denial, source unavailability, extraction failure, budget exhaustion, and verified negative evidence. Add deterministic fault-injection and benchmark cases for every status, verify retry versus terminal behavior, and test that user-facing abstention or explanation preserves the underlying cause.

gaps.description: An end-to-end cost evaluation covering retrieval calls, retrieved passages or tokens, planner or judge inference, reranking, permission-check latency, and total wall-clock latency remains absent from the admitted corpus.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve with end-to-end instrumentation and benchmarking. Record per-query retrieval calls, documents/passages/tokens fetched, planner and sufficiency-judge invocations and tokens, reranker work, authorization-check count and latency, generation cost, total wall-clock latency, and stopping iteration. Evaluate these metrics across fixed workloads and retrieval budgets so accuracy-risk-cost trade-offs can be compared reproducibly.

gaps.description: The corpus lacks a workplace-communication evaluation combining explicit evidence gaps with heterogeneous messages and documents, multi-hop dependencies, permission restrictions, stale or conflicting evidence, and bounded retrieval.
gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by constructing a workplace-communication benchmark or controlled testbed containing email/chat/document/attachment evidence, explicit evidence-gap annotations, multi-hop dependencies, ACL/IAM restrictions, versioned and stale records, deliberate conflicts, and retrieval budgets. Define expected evidence sets and stopping outcomes, then evaluate completeness, unsupported conclusions, permission leakage, temporal/version correctness, abstention behavior, retrieval cost, and latency.

gaps.description: No admitted study validates a single controller that jointly handles structured evidence gaps, permission-aware source access, version lineage, temporal validity, calibrated stopping, abstention, and total-cost budgeting; the reported successes remain component-level or cover smaller subsets of these functions.
gaps.suggested_search_query: "adaptive RAG controller" permission-aware provenance temporal version calibrated stopping abstention budget
gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-4. DynaKRAG and related controllers cover adaptive retrieval, sufficiency, stopping, or budgets, while other admitted studies separately cover permissions, temporal/version provenance, and conformal or calibrated risk control. No admitted study evaluates the complete controller specified by this gap.
